name: Malta

meta.title: Study in Malta from India: funds, work hours, post-study permit
meta.description: Study in Malta, an EU country. Malta's student fund rules in rupees, 20 hours of work a week after 90 days, and the 9-month post-study permit.

summary: An EU country with part-time work after 90 days and a 9-month permit to find a job after graduating.

whyReasons.text: After your first 90 days, you can work up to 20 hours a week while your student permit is valid.
After graduating (MQF level 5 or higher), you can apply for a one-time permit to stay up to 9 months to look for a job.

living.note: Minimum balance for the e-Residence Permit after you arrive. The University of Malta notes this does not fully cover accommodation and living costs.

visaFunds.text: For the long-stay visa, show at least 75% of Malta's national minimum wage for each month of study. After arrival, the e-Residence Permit needs a balance of at least €950 for each month of your stay, not counting tuition fees.

duringStudy.text: Up to 20 hours a week after the first 90 days, while your study residence permit is valid.

afterStudy.text: A one-time post-study residence permit of up to 9 months to look for a job, for graduates of MQF level 5 or higher courses in Malta.

faq.q: How much money do I need to show for Malta?
faq.a: For the visa, at least 75% of Malta's national minimum wage for each month of study. After you arrive, at least €950 for each month of your stay for the e-Residence Permit, not counting tuition.

faq.q: Can I work while studying in Malta?
faq.a: Yes, up to 20 hours a week after your first 90 days.

faq.q: Can I stay in Malta after my course?
faq.a: Graduates of MQF level 5 or higher courses can apply once for a permit of up to 9 months to look for a job.

faq.q: What does a master's in Malta cost?
faq.a: Fees depend on the institution and course. Your counsellor will give you the published fee for each course on your shortlist.
